educators.title: For educators
educators.heroTitle: Run a Thinkerwell lesson with your group
educators.heroBody: Every lesson works on one shared screen, in pairs, or on separate devices. There are no accounts to set up.
educators.need1: One device for every 1 to 3 learners, or one big screen
educators.need4: Internet for the first visit, and for videos
educators.step1Body: Lessons can go in any order. Choose one that fits your group, or follow the numbers.
educators.step2Body: Read, Write, Speak, Watch, Reflect. Pair learners for Speak. Watch can be skipped.
educators.step3Body: Ask two or three learners to share their answer. Everyone writes one reflection.
educators.previewIntro: Every lesson has a teacher guide with a session plan and the answers, and every section check has an answer key.
educators.answerKeyLabel: Answer key for the {section} section check
educators.codesBody: In the pilot, each learner can get a code like HLP-07. Later, codes will let us see how the whole group is doing, without any names. You keep the list that matches names to codes.
educators.feedbackBody: Something confusing, too hard, or broken? A video that does not play? Email us and we will fix it.

teacherGuide.intro: Everything you need to teach this lesson, with the answers. It prints on A4, black on white, without the menus.
teacherGuide.contentNotePointer: The video has a content note. Read it before class: it is with the video, below.
teacherGuide.planIntro: A suggested plan for a session of about 45 minutes. Change it to suit your group.
teacherGuide.planShorter: Only 30 minutes? Use the 30 min column: skip Watch or read instead, and take a little time off the other steps. Learners can open Watch later, because nothing is locked.

When it's on and this device can't turn speech into text by itself, Say it sends what learners say to the browser maker's online service (for example Google, Apple or Microsoft), and it needs the internet. Turn it on only if your organisation and the learners' families have agreed.

about.title: About Thinkerwell
about.tagline: Read with curiosity. Write with evidence. Speak with purpose. Watch with intention. Reflect and connect.
about.whatBody: Thinkerwell is a free social-studies course for young people across Southeast Asia, made with refugee, displaced and under-served learners in mind. Learners explore history, geography, culture and civic life through reading, writing, talking and reflecting.
about.whatHonesty: It is a student-led project, getting ready for its first pilot with a learning centre. It is not a registered charity.
about.promise1: It is free, with no adverts and no accounts.
about.promise2: We never ask about your past, your family or where you come from.
about.promise3: Your writing stays on your device. You choose what to share.
about.goalsTitle: The UN goals we work towards
about.goal4Body: Free social-studies learning for young people who face barriers to school.
about.goal10Body: Good learning materials for refugee, displaced and under-served youth.
about.goal16Title: Goal 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
about.goal16Body: History, civics and media skills, and the habit of respectful discussion.
about.goal16Alt: Sustainable Development Goal 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
about.goal17Body: Working with educators, youth networks and community groups.
about.goal17Alt: Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals
about.justinBio: Justin is a student in Singapore who loves history, sociology and Model United Nations. He started Thinkerwell because learning should not stop at borders, displacement or a lack of resources.
about.nickBio: Nick is a student in Singapore. He builds the Thinkerwell website and leads our work with AI. He is interested in how AI can help more people learn in their own language.
